Explicitly out of scope and untouched: go.mod/go.sum/.github/dependabot.yml/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md (owned by a parallel lane per this lane's own instructions), the full supply-chain.json/tools.lock graph (deferred per e1's review comment), egress block-mode rollout, and the apk closure sha256 (omitted -- see e1's D5 and the bug_fix event below).

Defect framed honestly: release-manifest.json signed source commit, workflow run, and output artifact digests (image/chart/binaries/sbom), but recorded none of the build INPUTS that produced them -- a verifier downloading a signed manifest had no way to tell which go.sum, which Go toolchain version, or which builder/runtime base image actually produced a given release, so a compromised or drifted build input was invisible to the one artifact designed to bind provenance together. Fix: a new 'Record build provenance' step in the release-binaries job (which already has Setup Go installed and the source checked out) captures `go version` (not the workflow's 'go-version: 1.26' input string -- the two can drift, as an earlier #26 comment found for golang 1.26 vs Dockerfile's 1.27 before that was fixed), sha256 of go.sum/go.mod, `git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}'`, and the builder/runtime image ref+digest parsed from Dockerfile's two `FROM ...@sha256:` lines (not hardcoded, so this can't drift from the image Dockerfile actually builds). Uploaded as an artifact (provenance-meta, same pattern as the existing checksums-bundle-meta/sbom-meta artifacts) and folded into release-manifest.json's new 'provenance' object BEFORE the existing cosign sign-blob step, so the extended manifest is what gets signed, not a subset of it. apk package closure sha256 is deliberately NOT recorded: /licenses/os-packages-manifest.txt only exists inside the built image, and the release-binaries job (where provenance is recorded) never builds/extracts that image -- the build-and-push job does, via multi-arch buildx with no local filesystem export cheap enough to read a file back out of. This follows e1's D5 (apk recorded via Syft SBOM, not pinned) one step further: it isn't even cheaply obtainable to record a digest of here, so it's omitted and documented as such rather than faked.

Ran `make release-manifest-local` against the actual working tree: built a real host-platform binary, packaged a real Helm chart, computed real sha256 of go.sum/go.mod, ran `go version`, parsed Dockerfile's two FROM lines, and assembled a schemaVersion-4 manifest. Iterated through two real Makefile bugs before it worked: (1) a `<(...)` process-substitution in a jq --slurpfile argument fails under Make's default /bin/sh (`syntax error near unexpected token '('`) -- replaced with writing the jq'd binaries array to a temp file first; (2) a multi-line jq filter string spanning several Makefile recipe lines without trailing backslash-continuation broke apart into separate shell invocations (`unexpected EOF while looking for matching '''`) -- collapsed the filter to one line. Then ran `python3 hack/verify-release.py --source . .release-manifest-local`: first pass correctly reported MISSING for compatibility-matrix.json (the local target hadn't copied it into the output dir yet -- fixed by adding that copy step), second pass OK on every check including the new provenance goSum/goMod checks against the real source tree.

events.summary: HIGH fix (e8, confirmed independently by e9): release.yaml's release-binaries job now runs scripts/ci/check-provenance-meta.sh (a new, standalone script -- the single source of truth for the required-fields shape, so the workflow and its own test never duplicate/drift the jq logic) against provenance-meta.json immediately after generating it, exiting the job before the artifact is ever uploaded if any required field is missing/empty or the JSON isn't an object. The release-manifest job re-runs the same check defensively right before the --slurpfile merge, in case the artifact were altered in transit between jobs. scripts/ci/test-check-provenance-meta.sh exercises the script directly against [], {}, a good fixture, and each required field removed individually -- runnable without a release. hack/verify-release.py's main() now computes provenance_shape_problems() for any schemaVersion >= 4 manifest and FAILs unconditionally (not gated behind --require-signatures) when provenance is missing, null, not an object, or any required field is missing/empty -- mirroring the exact same shape scripts/ci/check-provenance-meta.sh enforces upstream, so a manifest that passed the pipeline's own check always passes this one too.

MEDIUM fix (e8, e9 both raised it independently): hack/verify-release.py now verifies provenance.sourceCommit/sourceTreeHash against a real git checkout when --source is given, via a new git_rev_parse() helper (git -C <source> rev-parse <rev>, returns None rather than raising on anything that isn't a git checkout or lacks git on PATH). A resolvable checkout gets OK/MISMATCH treatment identical to the goSum/goMod checks; an unresolvable one (a plain extracted-tarball source snapshot, the common case for a downloaded release) prints SKIP with an explicit reason instead of silently doing nothing or crashing. Renamed provenance.goVersion to provenance.binaryGoVersion end to end (release.yaml's Record-build-provenance step, hack/verify-release.py, Makefile's release-manifest-local, CONTRIBUTING.md, all test fixtures) with an explicit comment/doc sentence at each site: it is the toolchain that compiled the three release binaries, not the container image's binary, which is a separate build using builderImage's own toolchain -- schemaVersion 4 is new in this same PR so there is no compatibility cost to the rename. binaryGoVersion/builderImage/runtimeImage now print under an explicit 'INFO (not verified):' prefix (was 'NOTE:'), and CONTRIBUTING.md's wording was corrected from 'this verifies' to naming exactly which fields ARE independently verified (goSum/goMod, sourceCommit/sourceTreeHash with --source) versus recorded-but-not-verified (binaryGoVersion, builder/runtime digests) -- no overclaiming.

LOW fixes (e9): a new _check_provenance_file() helper replaces direct entry['file']/entry['sha256'] indexing for goSum/goMod -- .get() plus an explicit FAIL message when either is absent, never an uncaught KeyError/traceback, and an explicit os.path.basename(file_name) == file_name rejection of any path separator in 'file' up front (belt-and-braces alongside safe_join's pre-existing realpath-containment check, which would already refuse a '../'-style escape but only after attempting to resolve it). test_default_mode_with_partial_manifests_is_unchanged's narrowed assertions (three exact excluded strings, from the original PR) were replaced with a KNOWN_SKIP_INFO_PREFIXES allowlist checked against every SKIP:/INFO line in the output -- any line not matching a known-good prefix now fails the test, restoring the original blanket assertion's strictness while still tolerating the one legitimate new provenance SKIP line.
